paragraphs: Swamiji once told of a devout Muslim who kept his daily prayers with great regularity. Whenever the hour of prayer arrived, wherever he happened to be, he would stop everything, kneel and bow to the ground. One day the call came while he was in a garden, so he spread himself out right there and began to pray.

In the same garden a young woman was waiting for the man she loved. Suddenly she spotted him on the far side. Her heart leapt, and she ran towards him so eagerly that she never noticed the man lying face down in her path. She simply stepped over him and kept going.

Now this worshipper was a rigid, fiery sort, the kind of believer who is sure that everyone else is headed for eternal punishment. Being walked over in the middle of his prayers made him furious, and he was ready to kill the girl.
But she was quick-witted and not easily frightened. She told him to stop his nonsense, and called him a fool and a hypocrite. Stunned, he demanded to know how he could be a hypocrite.

Her answer was simple. She had been running to meet a mere human beloved, and her mind was so full of him that she had not even seen a man lying on the ground. He, on the other hand, claimed to be meeting the Beloved of heaven itself, and yet he had felt every footstep on his back. If his heart had really been with God, how could he have noticed a girl passing over him?
learn: Real focus shows in what you stop noticing, not in how strictly you follow a routine. If you are easily distracted or offended in the middle of something you call important, it may be worth asking how much of your heart is actually in it.
